newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Asian currencies eye trade data.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Asian currencies eye trade data.

text.p: * Sing dollar firms on release of better-than-expected March non-oil trade data.
* Ringgit steadies against the dollar, eye on the February trade data due later in the week
* Liquidity softens the rupiah against the dollar
* Baht firms as the dollar weakens
Asian currencies were mostly range-bound in early Monday trade, subdued by expectations of a slew of economic data in various countries.
In Singapore, the Singapore dollar was range-bound at 1.4400/1.4415 to the dollar for most part of the morning.
However, the Singapore dollar broke 1.4400 to the dollar to 1.4395 after the release of a better-than-expected March non-oil export data at noon, dealers said.

According to the Trade Development Board (TDB), Singapore's non-oil domestic exports fell a nominal 2.1 percent year-on-year in March to Singapore $7.67 billion after falling 7.9 percent in February. In real term, it rose 0.5 percent to S$9.88 billion after falling 4.4 percent in February.
The figures were better than market expectations of an average fall of 4.5 percent in nominal terms.

Up north, the Malaysian ringgit was also steady to the dollar at 2.5060/70 after hitting 2.5130 earlier in the morning. Dealers in Singapore said focus was on Malaysia's February trade balance data due next week. They were expecting the figures to be much better than the 95.5 million gap in January.
However, dealers said the ringgit's upside appeared capped if the dollar/majors were to rise again.
The Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar in early trading.
"It's mainly the liquidity which is softening the rupiah," a local bank dealer in Jakarta said.
He added the dollar's uptrend was likely due to technicals following a new bank reserve requirement rate of five percent implemented last Wednesday.
Spot rupiah fell to 2,413.5/4.50 at 0400 GMT from an opening 2,410.5/11.5. Today rupiah dropped to 2,412.0/13.0 from 2,409.8/10.8 on ample selling. Tomorrow was at 2,412.4/12.9.
Some dealers said a relatively tight dollar market appeared to be another reason for the rupiah's weakening.
But the local dealer said the condition was only temporary because operators had established large long dollar positions last week on the back of the ample rupiah market.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,402/2,594 and the conversion band to 2,402/2,450 on Thursday.
The market was closed last Friday for a Muslim holiday.
The Thai baht firmed against the dollar as the greenback weakened abroad, dealers said.
Trading was also stymied by a series of Thai data, including the money supply and trade figures, expected to be released by mid-week.
The baht was quoted at 26.048/26.053 to the dollar against 26.072/26.077 late on Friday.
The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 26.06 per dollar compared with 26.08 on Friday.
"The baht is trading against the dollar at around 26.05. Some of those who have held long position in the dollar were seen selling," said one dealer.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), James Mclean in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Angela Tan in Singapore (65-8703083)
